Aria: Quick follow-up from the RFC — who owns the decision surface between observer signals and automatic fallback? We need a clear boundary before we start wiring this into Dedicated clusters.
Sam: Good question. The RFC left observer-runner as a thin layer, but ops raised concerns about ambiguity (who can trigger a hard fallback vs. a gentle degrade).
Jamal: From SRE side: prefer a single owner for actuation. Observer should only emit structured signals. Runner (runtime) should be the only component that executes fallbacks.
Priya: Agreed on single owner. My concern: signal schema and labels need to be stable so the runner's heuristics don't break on rollout.
Aria: Proposal sketch: observer -> emits events with fields {origin, signal_type, confidence, window_ms}. Runner consumes events, applies smoothing window + policy, then decides action (no-op / soft-degrade / hard-fallback). Example policy config: ```yaml
fallback_policy:
  name: default
  smoothing_window_ms: 15000
  min_action_ttl_ms: 60000
  buckets:
    - signal_type: latency_spike
      threshold: 0.75
      action: soft-degrade
    - signal_type: error_rate
      threshold: 0.2
      action: hard-fallback
```
Sam: Two follow-ups: 1) We need to avoid oscillations (so `min_action_ttl_ms` is critical). 2) The runner should be able to backoff to a degraded variant, not only binary fallback.
Jamal: Also add telemetry tags: `origin=observer`, `confidence=<0..1>`, `schema_version=v1`. Logs should look like: `runner:decision action=soft-degrade reason=latency_spike conf=0.82 window=15s`.
Priya: Ops runbook item: when fallback_count >= 3 within 10m for the same tenant, page SRE and switch canary to read-only mode. Suggest alert rule: ``alert:RepeatedFallbacks`` expr: `sum(fallbacks_total{job=runner,tenant!=""}[10m]) >= 3`.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: variant=v2 -> 5% traffic us-west at 2024-09-12T18:02:00Z :rocket:
Aria: For tests: unit tests that exercise runner policy boundaries + an e2e harness with `fake-observer` that can emit noisy signals. Also a chaos test that simulates observer lag.
Sam: I can own the runner impl and add smoothing primitives. I'll add canary feature flags so we can toggle strictness per deployment.
Jamal: I'll own the signal schema and publish it to the telemetry catalog. Will add compatibility rules for schema_version bumps.
Priya: I'll draft the runbook snippets and escalation paths. One more operational guard: if the observer stream is missing for >30s, runner should default to `defer` (no automatic fallback) to avoid blind actuation.
Aria: Nice. Action items: Sam -> implement smoothing + TTL; Jamal -> publish schema + migration notes; Priya -> runbook + alerts. Sam, please ping this thread when you have a prototype so we can run the e2e harness. :thumbsup:
